correctness.rationale: Finite birational normalization over an integral Cartier resultant hypersurface; conductor as finite-dual Hom; adjunction ratio O_N(0,1-n,1-m); irreducible residual resultant D gives Cartier multiplicity one at all points; reduced downstairs conductor follows from integral contraction of a radical ideal; the Euler polynomial follows from exact finite pushforward and hypersurface sequences. The actual packaged checker verified all reported finite examples, and the symbolic proof covers every m,n >=2.

value.rationale: The scheme-theoretic conductor is an intrinsic birational invariant with a direct geometric meaning. Its all-degree radicality on both source and target and the explicit twisted Euler polynomial of the normalization defect quantify nonnormality in a natural family and are not merely the classical generic-crossing observation. Useful for duality, adjunction, and Hilbert-polynomial calculations; no unsupported broader theorem is asserted.
